en: The Dharma Jewel of the Battle between the Deva Nārāyaṇa and the Asura King,
translated by Sīlavarman.
At that time, the Deva Nārāyaṇa was atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, having assembled the great devas.
There were also the Brahmā kings, the Great Maheśvara king, Śakra Devendra, and others;
as well as immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
There were also countless spirits and deities who gathered together to hear the Dharma being preached.
That ambrosial, wondrous medicine was then compounded and placed within a vial.
At that time, the Asura King transformed his appearance and entered the jar to consume the ambrosial,
wondrous medicine. Thereupon, Nārāyaṇa saw the Asura King enter the jar.
He tilted his golden wheel against the side of the jar,
whereupon half the body of the asura king was severed. Thus,
the asura became an afflicted one.
Take white mustard seeds, agallochum incense, sesame, ghee, and honey, and blend them together.
Take one hundred and eight pieces of khadira wood, each the length of a finger.
Recite the mantra once and burn [the incense] once,
while calling out the name of that person;
they shall immediately be cured.
Next, the mudrās are explained.
For the protection of the body:
interlace the two little fingers.
Within the palms, press the two ring fingers upon the little fingers; then,
extend the two middle fingers straight upward,
and pinch the backs of those two middle fingers with the two index fingers.
Press the two thumbs against the middle joints of the middle fingers;
turning three times to the right is called "protecting the body.
Thereafter, perform all ritual activities.
There is no obstruction.
This is the Sword Mudrā:
with the left hand, place the tip of the ring finger upon the upper joint of the index finger.
Press the thumbs upon the joints of the little fingers and ring fingers.
Hold the middle fingers and index fingers straight up. This is the wheel mudrā (*cakra-mudrā*).

Forming the "Wind-Emptiness" mudrā by joining the hands together so that they are round like a wheel, toss them upward three times toward the obstructed area and strike; thereby, all asuras shall be utterly severed.
Next is the Fire Seal (Agni-mudrā).
Form the vajra-fist with the left hand;
extend the five fingers of the right hand straight and move them slightly.
Supporting the left index finger against the center of the right palm, one can burn all *śatru*s (enemies).
By pointing the great flame of this mudrā toward them while visualizing them being consumed by fire, and likewise performing the *homa* sacrifice, one will certainly subdue the mothers (*mātṛ*).
On the fifth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of the Xiantong era, the bhikṣu Chan... [illegible character]... [illegible character].
